I found four papers in `library/llm/context/` that propose and test a remedy, plus one prompt-only fix. They change different things: the training data, the attention at inference, the position indices, or the prompt. All page numbers below come from the library's notes on each paper. I didn't reread the papers themselves this session.

### 1. Change the training data: FILM-7B (*Make Your LLM Fully Utilize the Context*)
- **Proposed cause:** long-context training gives too little explicit supervision for using details far from the question ([p. 1–2](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Make%20Your%20LLM%20Fully%20Utilize%20the%20Context.pdf?page=2)). The paper states this as a hypothesis and doesn't test it.
- **The change:** fine-tuning on synthetic questions over 4K–32K-token contexts made of shuffled ~128-token segments ([p. 3](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Make%20Your%20LLM%20Fully%20Utilize%20the%20Context.pdf?page=3)). Some questions depend on one segment, others on two or more that may lie far apart. The model is Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, fully fine-tuned. Inference is unchanged, but training costs about 300 GPU days ([p. 4](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Make%20Your%20LLM%20Fully%20Utilize%20the%20Context.pdf?page=4)).
- **Result:** on the authors' own position probes, the average across positions rises from 47.3 to 85.9. The gap between the best and worst position falls from 56.2 to 13.9 ([p. 6, Table 1](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Make%20Your%20LLM%20Fully%20Utilize%20the%20Context.pdf?dest=table.1&page=6)).
- **On real tasks:** the average over nine LongBench tasks goes from 30.6 to 39.9. The gain comes from question answering; summarisation barely moves (GovReport 33.3 → 33.8) ([p. 6–7, Table 2](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Make%20Your%20LLM%20Fully%20Utilize%20the%20Context.pdf?dest=table.2&page=6)).

### 2. Change the attention at inference: *Found in the Middle*
- **Proposed cause:** attention has a U-shaped bias by position, favouring the first and last documents whatever they contain ([p. 1](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Found%20in%20the%20Middle.%20Calibrating%20Positional%20Attention%20Bias%20Improves%20Long%20Context%20Utilization.pdf?page=1)). The paper models a document's attention as relevance plus a position bias plus noise.
- **The change:** the method measures the attention a dummy document gets at each position and subtracts it from each real document's attention at that position. What is left estimates relevance ([p. 5, Eq. 3–4](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Found%20in%20the%20Middle.%20Calibrating%20Positional%20Attention%20Bias%20Improves%20Long%20Context%20Utilization.pdf?page=5)). Attention over each document is then rescaled towards that relevance ([p. 6, Eq. 5–6](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Found%20in%20the%20Middle.%20Calibrating%20Positional%20Attention%20Bias%20Improves%20Long%20Context%20Utilization.pdf?page=6)).
- **Where it applies:** only the last 16 of 32 layers ([p. 13](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Found%20in%20the%20Middle.%20Calibrating%20Positional%20Attention%20Bias%20Improves%20Long%20Context%20Utilization.pdf?page=13)). There is no training, but it needs the model's internals and extra forward passes that grow with the number of documents ([p. 9](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Found%20in%20the%20Middle.%20Calibrating%20Positional%20Attention%20Bias%20Improves%20Long%20Context%20Utilization.pdf?page=9)).
- **Result:** accuracy with the answer in the middle rises by 6–15 points ([p. 6–7](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Found%20in%20the%20Middle.%20Calibrating%20Positional%20Attention%20Bias%20Improves%20Long%20Context%20Utilization.pdf?page=6)). For example, Vicuna on NaturalQuestions with 20 passages goes from 47.34 to 56.19.
- **Cost of the fix:** it loses where the uncorrected model was strongest. With the answer in the first passage, the same setup drops from 71.93 to 66.40 ([p. 13, Table 5](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Found%20in%20the%20Middle.%20Calibrating%20Positional%20Attention%20Bias%20Improves%20Long%20Context%20Utilization.pdf?dest=table.5&page=13)).
- **Caveats:** the authors call attention weights "not necessarily causal" ([p. 3](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Found%20in%20the%20Middle.%20Calibrating%20Positional%20Attention%20Bias%20Improves%20Long%20Context%20Utilization.pdf?page=3)) and say the bias's origin is unknown ([p. 9](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Found%20in%20the%20Middle.%20Calibrating%20Positional%20Attention%20Bias%20Improves%20Long%20Context%20Utilization.pdf?page=9)).

### 3. Change the position indices: STRING (*Why Does the Effective Context Length of LLMs Fall Short*)
- **Proposed cause:** large relative distances are rarely seen in training ([p. 3, Eq. 1–2](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Why%20Does%20the%20Effective%20Context%20Length%20of%20LLMs%20Fall%20Short.pdf?page=3)). In a sequence of length L, distance i occurs L − i times, so at L = 2048 the largest distance occurs once per sequence. Far-away tokens are therefore reached through poorly trained position indices.
- **The change:** at inference, the method drops the largest relative positions and shifts the rest so distant tokens get frequently trained indices. A small local window (W = 128) is kept so neighbours stay closest, and there is no training ([p. 6](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Why%20Does%20the%20Effective%20Context%20Length%20of%20LLMs%20Fall%20Short.pdf?page=6)).
- **Result:** at 128K tokens on the RULER benchmark, Llama3.1-70B goes from 66.6 to 81.7 and Qwen2-72B from 53.7 to 84.6. Llama3.1-8B gains only 77.0 → 80.0 ([p. 8, Table 2](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Why%20Does%20the%20Effective%20Context%20Length%20of%20LLMs%20Fall%20Short.pdf?dest=table.2&page=8)).
- **Caveat:** this paper doesn't strictly measure "lost in the middle." With the question at the end of inputs up to 128K tokens, models fail on evidence at the *start*, the part farthest from the question ([p. 5](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Why%20Does%20the%20Effective%20Context%20Length%20of%20LLMs%20Fall%20Short.pdf?page=5)). It is the same family of position bias but a different shape from the U-curve.

### 4. Change what enters the context, and its order: *LongLLMLingua*
- **The change:** a small model (LLaMA-2-7B) compresses the prompt with the question in mind before the call. It scores each document by how well it predicts the question and keeps the top ones ([p. 3, Eq. 2](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/LongLLMLingua.%20Accelerating%20and%20Enhancing%20LLMs%20in%20Long%20Context%20Scenarios%20via%20Prompt%20Compression.pdf?page=3)). It then sorts the kept documents by that score, so the most relevant come first ([p. 4, Eq. 4](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/LongLLMLingua.%20Accelerating%20and%20Enhancing%20LLMs%20in%20Long%20Context%20Scenarios%20via%20Prompt%20Compression.pdf?page=4)). The answering model is untouched, so this works with API models.
- **Result:** GPT-3.5-Turbo, uncompressed, scores 75.7 / 57.3 / 54.1 / 55.4 / 63.1 with the answer passage at position 1 / 5 / 10 / 15 / 20. With 4× compression it scores 75.0 / 71.8 / 71.2 / 71.2 / 74.7, and 75.5 with reordering ([p. 5, Table 1](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/LongLLMLingua.%20Accelerating%20and%20Enhancing%20LLMs%20in%20Long%20Context%20Scenarios%20via%20Prompt%20Compression.pdf?dest=table.1&page=5)).
- **What does the work:** most of the gain comes from the document scoring step. Without it, accuracy falls to 42.1 / 39.7 at the 1st / 10th position ([p. 6, Table 3](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/LongLLMLingua.%20Accelerating%20and%20Enhancing%20LLMs%20in%20Long%20Context%20Scenarios%20via%20Prompt%20Compression.pdf?dest=table.3&page=6)).

### Also: a prompt-only fix in *Lost in the Middle* itself
- **Repeat the question:** putting the question both before and after the data brings every model to near-perfect accuracy on the key–value lookup task. On multi-document question answering it barely changes the curve ([p. 7](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Lost%20in%20the%20Middle.%20How%20Language%20Models%20Use%20Long%20Contexts.pdf?page=7)).
- **Reorder or truncate:** the paper also suggests putting relevant documents near the start or cutting the ranked list short, but doesn't test this ([p. 9](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Lost%20in%20the%20Middle.%20How%20Language%20Models%20Use%20Long%20Contexts.pdf?page=9)).

### How the remedies compare
- **Model access:** the three model-side fixes (FILM-7B, Found in the Middle, STRING) need open weights. LongLLMLingua and the prompt changes work with API models.
- **No direct comparison:** each remedy was tested on its authors' own benchmark and on 7B–72B open models. No paper applies two of them to one model.
- **Cause unsettled:** whether the bias has one cause or several is still open.
- **Partial exception:** Found in the Middle compares itself with reordering, including LongLLMLingua's. On its synthetic dataset, calibration alone loses to reordering: Tulu with 20 passages scores 84.50 against 95.45 for LongLLMLingua's reordering ([p. 13, Table 5](http://pdf.invalid/llm/context/Found%20in%20the%20Middle.%20Calibrating%20Positional%20Attention%20Bias%20Improves%20Long%20Context%20Utilization.pdf?dest=table.5&page=13)).

I didn't change any files, so there is nothing to commit.
